topic: DSH Tianshu TUI: Interactive Terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness

key_points: Official DeepSeek Harness interactive terminal UI plugin (npm @huiliyi37/dsh-tianshu-tui, Apache-2.0, 158 stars, created 2026-08-13)
Rendering core evolved from Tianshu-Tui; pure display layer — all agent state derived from session event stream, TUI registers no prompts/tools/context
Harness-engineering personalizations: TDD-driven workflow, evidence gate, image/vision bridge, code intelligence retrieval, memory & cross-session recall
Requires official CLI @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.0-rc.6; Node ^22.19 || >=24 and pnpm; install via `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile tui add @huiliyi37/dsh-tianshu-tui`
Full in-terminal workspace: live rendering, session restore, /fork, /rewind, /export Markdown, /steer mid-turn steering
End-to-end images: clipboard paste, inline render via kitty/iTerm2 graphics protocol, vision bridge auto-detects when main model can't see images
Complete input surface: grok-style slash menu, @-path tab completion, bracketed paste, optional vim keys, external editor (Ctrl+E), history search (Ctrl+F)
Reasoning visualization: think channel streams live, folds to compact rows, Ctrl+O expands inline
Personalized harness integration: /doctor diagnostics, /memory project memory browser, /btw background agent, /model + /effort hot-switch

Co-evolves with harness (250+ commits 2026-08-10 to 08-13): image/vision chain, DeepSeek Spark model engineering, session persistence & file snapshots, memory, evidence gate & failure routing, code intelligence, git tools
Full-featured, high-performance terminal coding agent runtime (TUI), 229 stars, 21 forks, TypeScript, Apache-2.0, created 2026-06-09
Built on Cognitive Virtual Machine (CVM), self-awareness layer, and Stigmergy (pheromone) self-decaying memory — treats models as partners, not tools
DeepSeek V4 prefix-cache engineering optimization: steady-state hit rate 95-99% in long sessions
13,000+ tests passed; dev codename Rivet, CLI command still `rivet`; npm package tianshu-tui
Desktop builds (macOS .dmg, Windows .msi, Linux .AppImage) plus npm global install; Windows needs WebView2 Runtime
Git unlocks delegation worktree isolation, checkpoint rollback, commit/diff review, per-worker diff review
Terminal-native agent UI for DeepSeek Harness built in Rust/ratatui, MIT, 25 stars, npm @openma/deepseek-harness-tui
Runs as official dsh profile plugin or connects directly to SDK JSON-RPC runtime
Complete agent timeline: streaming reasoning, replies, tool params/results, plugin context, subagent lifecycle, token/cache metrics
Multi-image prompt: stage up to 8 images from file/clipboard/paste as editable [image n] chips
Terminal-friendly Markdown rendering preserving CJK/Latin mixed layout; high-density tool view with collapsible results
Long-conversation controls: queue follow-ups, interrupt, persistent JSONL sessions via /new, /resume, --session-id
Cross-platform input: readline editing, macOS ⌘/⌥ fixes, Linux/Windows ctrl combos; dark/light themes, narrow-screen layout
Thin, readable Ink (React for terminals) plugin ~800 lines of UI — not a re-implementation of the harness, 7 stars, JavaScript
Terminal-native, zero-chrome: transcript is the surface, no boxes; DeepSeek brand banner only on empty state
Tool calls fold into cells: spinner while active, then ✓/✗ with duration, output merged/dimmed/truncated head+tail
Theme derived from your terminal via OSC 11 probe (12% white over dark, 4% black over light), never hardcoded hex
Thinking folding via ctrl+t; esc interrupts running turn; /help lists keys and commands
Requires Node ≥20, a TokenDance API key, and dsh install; run `dsh --profile tui`
One-stop DeepSeek Harness community distribution: Desktop, Web, and TUI three forms unified, 188 stars, 14 forks, TypeScript, MIT
Single `ohdsh` command launches Desktop, Web, or TUI; three ends share sessions, credentials, skins, plugin cache with independent profiles
Local dev workbench: Workspace, PTY terminal, browser, file browser, Side chat, Trajectory; panels collapsible/fixed/split/fullscreen
Git Review: view workspace changes and commit diffs, add review comments on code lines, branch/commit/push from same sidebar
Plugin marketplace: browse, categorize, install, enable, update, uninstall; changes go to isolated preview first, reversible
Cross-end skins via @oh-dsh/skins providing unified theme adapted per interface

stats.fact: Official DeepSeek Harness (deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) has 111,829 stars and 10,833 forks as of 2026-08-15; tagline 'Everything is a Plugin'
dsh-tianshu-tui (the reviewed plugin) has 158 stars and 6 forks, created 2026-08-13, latest npm release @huiliyi37/dsh-tianshu-tui@0.1.2-rc.7 (2026-08-15)
Tianshu-Tui (the rendering core) reports 13,000+ passing tests and DeepSeek V4 prefix-cache steady-state hit rate of 95-99% in long sessions
Tianshu-Tui has 229 stars and 21 forks, created 2026-06-09, Apache-2.0, TypeScript
dsh-tianshu-tui co-evolved with the harness over 250+ commits between 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-13 on the 2026-08-09 baseline snapshot
The plugin requires official CLI @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.0-rc.6, Node.js ^22.19 || >=24, and pnpm on PATH
openma-ai/deepseek-harness-tui (Rust/ratatui) supports staging up to 8 images per prompt and runs as a dsh profile plugin or against the SDK JSON-RPC runtime
oh-dsh (hust-open-atom-club) packages DSH runtime into Desktop, Web, and TUI distributions with a shared plugin marketplace and Git Review

angles: The 'Everything is a Plugin' philosophy: how dsh-tianshu-tui is a pure display layer that derives all state from the session event stream, unlike monolithic AI IDEs
Prefix-cache engineering as the hidden cost lever: 95-99% hit rate in long sessions and what it means for token cost and latency on DeepSeek V4
Terminal-native vs IDE: why a TUI (not a GUI) is the natural home for harness-style agent workflows — zero chrome, scriptable, git-native
The vision bridge pattern: how a text-only main model can still 'see' images via an auto-detected auxiliary vision model, with graceful degradation
TDD/evidence-gate workflow: RED-first verification, obligation state machine, and failure routing as a differentiator from plain chat UIs
The ecosystem race: comparing the 5+ community TUI implementations (TypeScript/Ink, Rust/ratatui, oh-dsh multi-form) and what each optimizes for
Memory & cross-session recall: Stigmergy self-decaying memory and /memory project browser as the shift from stateless chat to persistent agent partner
Install friction as a review angle: the ERR_FS_EISDIR / stale-dsh pitfalls and why the official CLI version pin (0.1.0-rc.6) matters
